name: Generation Collab!

pick.label: Pick a brand
pick.heading: Pick a brand and find it a partner from another generation
lead: Some brands are loved by your grandparents, some by your parents and some only by people under 25. Every now and then two of them get together, and the results are either wonderful or very confusing.
Choose a brand from the shelf, or bring your own, then pair it with a brand from a different generation and launch something together. *The bigger the age gap, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a real marketing plan here, this is just for a bit of fun. The best collabs make your grandma and your little brother want exactly the same thing.

rows: Which brand from the shelf (or your own) are you starting with?
A brand from a different generation. The bigger the age gap, the better.
What exactly is it? A product, a shop, an app, an event?
Who buys it first: grandparents, grandchildren, or both together?
One line that works for an 18-year-old and an 80-year-old.
Where and how? Who do you get to talk about it?

values.product: The Night Owl: a caramel in a black wrapper, handed out only at the door of Berghain at 5am. Anyone over 70 skips the queue.
values.who: Grandparents who have always wondered what goes on in there, and clubbers who need sugar and a bit of comfort at 5am.
values.slogan: Sweet dreams are made of this.
values.launch: A video of my neighbour Gisela, 81, getting into Berghain on her first try. I have been turned away three times. She will never let me forget it.

yours.label: Your collab
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your collab in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which collab wins?
rank.placeholder: The collab, e.g. The Night Owl
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their collab in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
